accuracy.evidence: Matches the topic statement and its CCSS anchors W.K.7-W.2.7 (participate in shared research and writing projects) and W.K.8-W.2.8 (recall information from experiences or gather information from provided sources to answer a question). Hedgehog facts were checked against the British Hedgehog Preservation Society: they eat beetles, caterpillars, earthworms and slugs, forage at night, hibernate over winter, carry thousands (about 5,000-7,000) of spines, and the young are called hoglets. The story-book card is labelled as made up, so no false fact is presented as true.

misconceptions.evidence: Targets the slips teachers report in early research: a topic word or an opinion question used as the research question (step 1, prediction 1, challenge topic/opin), a story book trusted as a factual source (prediction 2, the magnifier step, p3), keeping every true fact even when it does not answer the question (the fit sort, p2, m6), copying whole sentences as notes (prediction 3, m3), and repeating a fact or adding an opinion to the shared writing (poster step, p4, m5).

lab_distinct.evidence: The mechanics follow the research cycle itself: choosing among a topic word, an opinion question and a researchable question; dragging a magnifier over four sources that reveal useful or made-up; sorting facts by relevance to one fixed question; tapping key words inside a source sentence to build a notes strip; and filing classmates' cards onto a poster or a leave-off tray for repeats and opinions. Shingle gate passed against all flagship labs, including flag_topic, flag_fvo and flag_book.

lab_teaches.evidence: Each step makes the child apply one research move and get told why: the wrong questions explain what is missing, the story book is rejected because it is made up, true-but-off-question facts are kept aside, the notes strip shows how few words are needed, and the poster refuses a repeat and an opinion. The text then names the move: research question, source, relevant fact, notes, share.

predictions.evidence: Three locked predictions with tempting wrong options: 'Yes, it is a question' for Hedgehogs, 'Yes, it is in a book' for the story-book cake (disproved when the magnifier shows 'made up'), and 'every word copied out' for good notes (disproved by the three-word notes strip).

challenge_feedback.evidence: Six rotating questions with twelve tagged messages: topic not a question, opinion question, story as source, colouring page has no facts, two off-question facts (jumping, colour), whole-sentence copying, small words as key words, a repeated fact, dropping a real fact, believing only books count, and calling a sighting an opinion.

readability.evidence: Kid text sits within the family limit (grade 5) with short sentences built around one example (what do hedgehogs eat?); canvas labels are a few words with emoji for each source, and every canvas action has a large button. Adult text stays within grade 10 and uses the standard terms research question, source, fact, non-fiction, notes and key words.

no_filler.evidence: Passed the filler regex and the 12% duplicate gate against every lesson, including Main Topic of Informational Texts and Fact vs opinion. Kid paragraphs each add one stage of the cycle; adult paragraphs give the standards, the cycle, the five common mistakes and the lab outline.

mobile.evidence: Checked iPhone and 360 px Android screenshots of every step in light and dark: the three question cards stack full width, the four sources sit in a 2 x 2 grid above the magnifier, the fact card sits above two side-by-side boxes, the nine words wrap three per row above the notes strip, and the poster and leave-off tray sit side by side under the incoming card. Young-class buttons are 56 px.

accessibility.evidence: walk.cjs: every task completes with Show me on desktop and iPhone 13, the challenge shows, axe WCAG 2.1 AA is clean in both themes, no console errors. Each drag or tap has a button route (question buttons, 'Check' source buttons, Answers it / Not about food, one button per word, Add to poster / Leave it off) and the canvas aria-label says what was found after each move.

sources: Common Core State Standards for English Language Arts, Writing W.K.7, W.1.7, W.2.7 (shared research and writing projects) and W.K.8, W.1.8, W.2.8 (recall information from experiences or gather information from provided sources to answer a question)
Department for Education (2013), National Curriculum in England: English programmes of study, Years 3-4 reading (retrieve and record information from non-fiction)
British Hedgehog Preservation Society, 'Hedgehog facts' and 'Feeding hedgehogs' advice leaflets (diet of beetles, caterpillars, worms and slugs; nocturnal; hibernation; 5,000-7,000 spines; hoglets)
